respaldo.emergencia: Follow the spacecraft's emergency protocol now and tell the crew and the flight surgeon immediately.
respaldo.estado: Your overall status today is {puntaje} of 100. {motivo}
respaldo.aviso: When to call the flight surgeon: {aviso}
respaldo.sinValor: I have no measurements of {nombre} yet; you can measure it with the vest or log it.
respaldo.prediccion: Based on your data, it could leave your normal in {n} days.
respaldo.medicoNada: No zone is outside your normal; keep your routine and report any symptoms.
respaldo.noEntiendo: I can explain your status today, a body zone, an indicator or how to measure yourself with the vest.
respaldo.noDiagnostico: I can't diagnose diseases; I only compare your data with your normal.
respaldo.noMedicamento: I don't prescribe medication or doses: the flight surgeon decides that.
respaldo.sinInternet: I don't have internet; I explain with what is on board.
respaldo.noInvento: I don't make up values. Here is your real {nombre} series; if a day is missing, you can measure or log it.
respaldo.otroTripulante: I only have the data of the active crew member ({tripulante}). To see someone else, switch in the profile.
respaldo.agendaCompleta: You already did everything on today's schedule.
respaldo.animo: Thanks for telling me; feeling this way on a long mission is normal. Logging your mood today helps see if it changes. Talk to someone in the crew or to the psychological support team.
respaldo.comparar: Here are {a} and {b} together. Moving at the same time doesn't prove one causes the other.
respaldo.radiacion: {nombre}: {valor}, {porcentaje} % of your career limit of {limite} mSv ({fuente}).
respaldo.repetirMedicion: If the value surprises you, fix that and repeat the measurement before drawing conclusions.

frases.sinReferencia: {nombre} {valor}; no reference to compare with yet.
frases.metaDias: {nombre}: {dias} days in a row below the {meta} goal (yesterday: {valorAyer}).
frases.sinMediciones: There are no measurements for this zone yet.
frases.dentroDeTuNormal: Your indicators are within your normal.

nervios.funcion: Carries signals between the brain and the body.

corazon.funcion: Pumps blood to the whole body.

metabolismo.funcion: Turns food into energy and regulates glucose.

rinones.funcion: Filter the blood (risk of kidney stones in space).

vascular.funcion: Carries the blood; changes with gravity.

huesos.funcion: Support the body; lose density in microgravity.

musculos.funcion: Move the body; waste away without load.

piel_inmune.funcion: First barrier; reflects fever and immune changes.

textos.queEs: How many times your heart beats per minute at rest.
textos.queSignifica: A resting pulse above your normal can signal fatigue, dehydration or stress.
textos.porQueEspacio: Microgravity shifts fluids toward the chest and changes how hard the heart works.

acciones: Rest for 10 minutes and repeat the measurement.
Drink water.
Check your hours of sleep.
pulso_reposo.avisoMedico: If it stays outside your normal for 48 h or you feel dizzy or have chest pain.

textos.queEs: How much the time between one heartbeat and the next varies.
textos.queSignifica: Variability lower than your normal often comes with tiredness or built-up stress.
textos.porQueEspacio: The mission schedule, noise and isolation shift the balance between rest and alertness.

acciones: Do 5 minutes of slow breathing.
Cut back on intense work today.
Repeat the measurement tomorrow when you wake up.
hrv.avisoMedico: If it stays below your normal 3 days in a row or comes with palpitations.

textos.queEs: The pressure of blood in your arteries when the heart beats.
textos.queSignifica: A change from your normal means your circulation is adapting to gravity or effort.
textos.porQueEspacio: Without gravity, blood redistributes and the body adjusts pressure; back in gravity it can drop when you stand up.

acciones: Sit for 5 minutes and repeat the measurement.
Drink water.
Stand up slowly if you feel dizzy.
presion_sistolica.avisoMedico: If it stays outside your normal for 2 measurements in a row or you have dizziness, blurred vision or a strong headache.

textos.queEs: The pressure of blood in your arteries between heartbeats.
textos.queSignifica: A change from your normal means your circulation is adapting.
textos.porQueEspacio: Fluid redistribution in microgravity changes the tone of the blood vessels.

acciones: Sit for 5 minutes and repeat the measurement.
Drink water.
presion_diastolica.avisoMedico: If it stays outside your normal for 2 measurements in a row or you have a strong headache.

textos.queEs: What percentage of your blood is carrying oxygen.
textos.queSignifica: A value lower than your normal means less oxygen is reaching your blood.
textos.porQueEspacio: The spacecraft atmosphere and cabin pressure changes affect oxygenation.

acciones: Breathe deeply and slowly for 2 minutes and repeat the measurement.
Check that the sensor is placed correctly.
Tell the crew if the cabin has air alarms.
spo2.avisoMedico: If it drops below 92 %, or you are short of breath, have bluish lips or feel confused.

textos.queSignifica: A temperature above your normal can mean your body is responding to something.
textos.porQueEspacio: During a mission the immune system changes and some latent viruses can reactivate.

acciones: Rest and drink water.
Repeat the measurement in 1 hour.
Note any other symptoms.
temperatura.avisoMedico: If it reaches 38.5 °C or stays high for more than 24 h.

textos.queEs: The amount of sugar circulating in your blood.
textos.queSignifica: A value outside your normal means a change in how you use energy from food.
textos.porQueEspacio: Relative inactivity and the mission diet change how the body uses glucose.

acciones: Review what and when you ate.
Repeat the measurement 2 hours after eating.
Keep up your exercise routine.
glucosa.avisoMedico: If it goes above 250 mg/dL, or you have intense thirst, dizziness or confusion.

textos.queEs: How many hours you slept last night.
textos.queSignifica: Sleeping little several nights in a row lowers attention and mood.
textos.porQueEspacio: Artificial light, noise and shifts disrupt the body clock during a mission.

acciones: Plan 8 hours of sleep tonight.
Avoid screens 30 minutes before bed.
Use an eye mask and earplugs if there is light or noise.
sueno_horas.avisoMedico: If you sleep less than 5 hours 3 nights in a row or notice confusion.

textos.queEs: How you feel today, from 1 (very bad) to 5 (very good).
textos.queSignifica: Several days of low mood deserve attention and support.
textos.porQueEspacio: Isolation, distance from home and a closed routine affect mood on long missions.

acciones: Talk with someone on the crew.
Schedule a call or message home.
Spend 20 minutes on something you enjoy.
animo.avisoMedico: If your mood stays low for 3 days or you have thoughts that worry you.

textos.queEs: How long you take to respond to a signal in the 60-second test.
textos.queSignifica: A time slower than your normal often reflects tiredness or lack of sleep.
textos.porQueEspacio: Fatigue, CO₂ and irregular sleep affect attention during a mission.

acciones: Rest for 15 minutes and repeat the test.
Avoid precision tasks until you repeat it.
Check your hours of sleep.
tiempo_reaccion.avisoMedico: If it stays slower than your normal for 2 tests in a row or you notice confusion.

textos.queEs: Your body mass measured with the spacecraft's device.
textos.queSignifica: Losing mass steadily means you are eating less than you burn.
textos.porQueEspacio: During a mission appetite tends to drop and daily exercise raises energy use.

acciones: Finish all of today's meals.
Add a snack between meals.
Log what you eat for 3 days.
masa_corporal.avisoMedico: If you have lost more than 5 % since the start of the mission.

textos.queEs: Minutes of resistance exercise you did today.
textos.queSignifica: Missing the goal several days in a row speeds up bone and muscle loss.
textos.porQueEspacio: Without the load of gravity, bones and muscles weaken; daily exercise protects them.

acciones: Finish today's exercise session.
Split the exercise into two blocks if it is hard.
Prioritize loaded exercises.
ejercicio_min.avisoMedico: If you cannot exercise because of pain or dizziness.

textos.queEs: The concentration of carbon dioxide in the cabin air.
textos.queSignifica: High cabin CO₂ can cause headaches and lower concentration.
textos.porQueEspacio: In a closed spacecraft CO₂ builds up if the removal systems cannot keep up.

acciones: Tell the crew to check CO₂ removal.
Move to a module with better ventilation.
Avoid intense exercise until it drops.
co2_cabina.avisoMedico: If you have a headache, dizziness or trouble concentrating while CO₂ is high.

textos.queEs: The total radiation you have received during your career.
textos.queSignifica: The closer you are to the career limit, the more it matters to protect yourself in each solar event.
textos.porQueEspacio: Away from Earth there is no magnetic field or thick atmosphere to stop radiation.

acciones: Follow the shelter plan if there is a solar alert.
Always wear your dosimeter.
Spend less time outside the shielded areas.
dosis_radiacion.avisoMedico: If you get close to 80 % of your budget or feel nauseous after a solar event.

textos.queSignifica: A high daily dose is usually caused by a solar particle event.
textos.porQueEspacio: Solar storms can multiply in hours the dose of several days.

acciones: Go to the shielded shelter and follow the solar event protocol.
Keep your dosimeter on.
Drink water and rest.
tasa_dosis_dia.avisoMedico: If today's dose goes over the limit or you have nausea, vomiting or intense fatigue.

textos.queEs: How much your head hurts, from 0 (none) to 3 (a lot).
textos.queSignifica: A headache can come from the cabin environment, sleep or hydration.
textos.porQueEspacio: In microgravity fluids rise to the head and cabin CO₂ can add discomfort.

acciones: Check the cabin CO₂.
Drink water and rest for 20 minutes.
Cut down on screens and bright light.
cefalea.avisoMedico: If the pain is intense, comes on suddenly or comes with blurred vision or confusion.

textos.queEs: How dizzy you feel, from 0 (not at all) to 3 (a lot).
textos.queSignifica: Dizziness often appears when gravity or blood pressure changes.
textos.porQueEspacio: The inner ear and circulation adapt when moving from microgravity to gravity.

acciones: Sit or lie down until it passes.
Stand up slowly.
Drink water.
mareo.avisoMedico: If the dizziness is strong, does not improve with rest or you faint.

textos.queEs: Whether you have irritation, a rash or wounds on your skin, from 0 (none) to 3 (a lot).
textos.queSignifica: Skin changes can reflect irritation or an immune system response.
textos.porQueEspacio: Skin dries out and heals more slowly during a mission; the immune system changes too.

acciones: Clean and dry the area.
Use the moisturizing cream from the medical kit.
Photograph the area to compare tomorrow.
lesion_piel.avisoMedico: If the lesion grows, oozes, hurts a lot or a fever appears.

tarjeta.queSignifica: Several signals changed at once and often come with built-up tiredness.
acciones: Make 8 hours of sleep a priority tonight.
Cut back on intense work today.
Repeat pulse and variability tomorrow when you wake up.
tarjeta.avisoMedico: If it does not improve in 48 h or you have dizziness, chest pain or confusion.
tarjeta.porQueEspacio: Isolation, irregular schedules and artificial light disrupt sleep during a mission.

co2_sintomas.nombre: Symptoms likely caused by the environment

tarjeta.queSignifica: The headache coincides with high cabin CO₂; the cause is likely environmental.
acciones: Tell the crew to check CO₂ removal.
Move to a module with better ventilation.
Drink water and rest for 20 minutes.
tarjeta.avisoMedico: If the pain continues once CO₂ is back to normal, or confusion or blurred vision appears.
tarjeta.porQueEspacio: In a closed spacecraft CO₂ builds up and can cause headaches even at moderate levels.

riesgosDestacados: Space radiation without a planet's protection
Microgravity: fluids shift toward the head
Vibration and fatigue on long drives
Lunar dust on skin and airways
Partial gravity: less load on bones and muscles
Adapting to partial gravity after the journey

normal.descripcion: All indicators within their personal normal.

deterioro_sueno.descripcion: Sleep hours drop over four nights and mood falls by one point.

multisenal_fatiga.descripcion: Resting pulse rises, heart rate variability drops and sleep is short at the same time.

co2_alto_cefalea.descripcion: Cabin CO₂ exceeds the limit for a day and a headache appears.

evento_solar.descripcion: A solar storm raises today's dose and the cumulative radiation.

preparacion_aterrizaje.descripcion: Blood pressure drops gradually, mild dizziness appears and exercise is cut in half.

pasos: This is your wrist sensor: it measures pulse, variability and oxygen.
Place it on your left wrist, two fingers above the bone.
Adjust the strap: firm, not tight. The sensors must touch the skin.
Keep still and breathe normally for 60 seconds.
Done. Watch your heart update on the 3D body.
erroresComunes: Sensor over the wrist bone: the reading is unstable.
Measuring right after moving: wait 5 minutes at rest.

pasos: This cuff measures blood pressure and glucose.
Place it on your left arm, at heart level.
Adjust it so one finger fits between the cuff and the skin.
Rest your arm, do not talk and wait until it finishes.
Done. Check your vascular system on the 3D body.
erroresComunes: Cuff on the forearm: the pressure reads higher than it really is.

pasos: This sensor measures your body temperature without lasting contact.
Bring it to the center of your forehead.
Hold it 1 cm from the skin, with no hair or sweat in between.
Wait for the reading-complete signal.
Done. Check your skin and immunity on the 3D body.
erroresComunes: Sensor too far from the forehead: the temperature reads lower.

pasos: This dosimeter records the radiation you receive during the day.
Clip it to the center of your chest, over your clothes.
Check that the sensor face points outward.
Wear it all day; your dose is added up at the end.
Done. The halo shows your radiation budget.
erroresComunes: Dosimeter kept in a pocket or drawer: it does not record your real exposure.

pasos: Moisten the electrodes: a drop of water on each ECG electrode improves skin contact.
Put the vest on snugly: close to the body without restricting breathing, with the band at sternum level.
Clip the oximeter on your index finger, clean and warm. Wait for the light to settle.
Keep the dosimeter in the chest pocket, also while you sleep.
Stay still for 60 seconds: the first resting reading sets your value for the day.
Done. Watch your heart update on the 3D body.
erroresComunes: Loose vest: the sensors move and read noise.
erroresPasos: Dry electrodes: the pulse signal gets lost.
Loose vest: the sensors move and read noise.
Cold finger or dark nail polish: SpO₂ reads low without being low.
Dosimeter away from the body: the recorded dose is not yours.
Measuring right after exercise: a high pulse triggers a false alert.

ecg.donde: Chest, below the left collarbone and over the ribs

respiracion.donde: Around the chest, at sternum level
